question: If the projection of $\vec{a} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}$ on $\vec{b} = 4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$ is 3 and $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b} + \hat{j}$, find all the possible ordered pairs $(x, y)$.
explanation:
First, projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}$:

$\dfrac{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|} = 3$

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 4x - 3y$

$|\vec{b}| = 5$

$\implies 4x - 3y = 15$ (1)

Now $\vec{a} \perp (\vec{b} + \hat{j}) = (4\hat{i} - 2\hat{j})$

$\vec{a} \cdot (4\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}) = 4x - 2y = 0$

$\implies 4x = 2y \implies x = y/2$

Plug into (1):

$4(y/2) - 3y = 15$

$2y - 3y = 15 \implies -y = 15 \implies y = -15$, $x = -15/2$

So only possible pair is $(-7.5, -15)$.
